note.explanation: Scientific notation writes a number as a value from 1 to 9 multiplied by a power of 10. The power shows how far, and in which direction, the decimal point moved.
note.simple: Move the decimal point until one non-zero digit is left of it. Moving left gives a positive power; moving right gives a negative power.
note.title: Writing numbers in scientific notation
steps: Move the decimal point until one non-zero digit remains on the left.
Count the places the decimal point moved.
Use that count as the exponent of 10: positive if the decimal moved left, negative if it moved right.
note.answer: A number written as a number from 1 to 9 multiplied by a power of 10.

examTips: This section is commonly tested with short numerical problems: write a number in scientific notation, or add, subtract, multiply, or divide numbers in scientific notation.
For addition and subtraction, show that the powers of 10 have been made the same before combining coefficients.
For multiplication, multiply the coefficients and add the exponents; for division, divide the coefficients and subtract the exponents.
Show the normalization step when a coefficient is not between 1 and 9, and include the final unit. These working steps can earn marks even if the final arithmetic has an error.

explain.title: What scientific notation means
explain.body: It is short way of representing very large or very small numbers. The numerical part of the quantity is written as a number from 1 to 9 multiplied by whole number powers of 10.

explain.title: Writing a large number
explain.body: To write numbers using scientific notation, move the decimal point until only one non-zero digit remains on the left. Count the places moved: moving the decimal to the left gives a positive exponent of 10. For example, 138,000,000 km = 1.38 × 10⁸ km.

explain.title: Writing a small number
explain.body: For a small number, move the decimal point to the right until one non-zero digit remains on the left. The number of places moved to the right is expressed as a negative exponent of 10. For example, 0.000,000,000,052 m = 5.2 × 10⁻¹¹ m.

explain.title: Calculating with powers of 10
explain.body: For addition or subtraction, first write the terms with the same power of 10. For multiplication, multiply the coefficients and add the exponents. For division, divide the coefficients and subtract the denominator exponent from the numerator exponent.

mistakes: Using a positive exponent when the decimal point moved to the right, or a negative exponent when it moved to the left.
Adding or subtracting coefficients before making the powers of 10 equal.
Forgetting to add exponents in multiplication or subtract exponents in division.
Leaving a coefficient such as 24 or 0.35 in the final answer instead of normalizing it to a value from 1 to 9.
Dropping the unit or giving an incorrect unit after multiplying or dividing quantities.
